title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 76
paragraphs: Having delivered this message, he slipped away. The Persians, thinking the report deserved credit, first landed a large contingent of their own men on the small island of Psyttaleia, which lies between Salamis and the mainland; and then, as midnight approached, they put the western wing of their fleet to sea, circling around toward Salamis. Those stationed about Keos and Kynosura also launched their ships, and they occupied the whole strait with their vessels as far as Munychia. The reason they put their ships out was so that the Greeks would not even be allowed to escape, but, cut off at Salamis, would pay the price for the battles at Artemisium. They landed Persian troops on the little island of Psyttaleia for this reason: that when the fight took place, these men might save their own side's survivors and kill those of the other, since that island especially was where men and wreckage were likely to be cast up on shore, lying as it did in the path of the coming sea-battle. All this they did in silence, so that the enemy should not have word of it.
